_about: Every sentence, clause and table cell of GUIDON_COMMAND_LEGAL_PACKAGE.md, in document order, each with a stable id and either a reason it is not a factual claim or how it is verified. Read by tools/verify-legal-package.mjs (static check in npm run lint:patterns; --run executes the proofs). Ids never change once assigned; a new sentence takes the next free number and is placed where it sits in the document. kind: factual | non-factual. verification: mechanical (named tests assert it) | partial (tests prove part; 'gap' says what a human must check) | unverifiable (no repository test can check it; 'class' and 'reason') | contradicted (the running app disagrees; 'finding'). A proof names a test (an npm script) and either an anchor (words from the assertion in the test that proves it) or, for the tagged suites written for this tool, the claim's own [LP-nnn] tag. Never map a claim to a test that does not assert it.

test:opsec-guard.about: MOI Import and the Squad Roster driven through the real built page against tools/fixtures/opsec-guard-cases.json, plus a sweep of the app's own content for false stops.

test:opsec-harmonization.about: The merged content bank and the runtime modules read without a build: the guard fixture table, the curriculum's counts, the network-boundary wording in studygroup.js and guest.html, and the MOI import order.

test:opsec-curriculum.about: The Cybersecurity & OPSEC screen through the real page: dictionary meanings kept, no duplicate prompts, the 10-question self-check, Open in Train.

test:guest-page.about: dist/guest.html served over plain http by the reference room host to a real browser: the boundary and not-endorsed notices in every state, nothing stored, joins and scores.

test:privacy.about: Backups leave out the squad roster by default; the in-app privacy text equals PRIVACY.md; the study-groups switch defaults off; the offline check reads the connection ledger.

test:standalone.about: The standalone file opened from file:// walks every route with zero external requests; study groups are off and inert in it.

test:room-privacy.about: Study rooms with the switch off refuse to connect and record nothing; with it on, exactly one ledger entry per page and no study data in any frame.

test:legal-package-guard.about: Every marking shape, identifier, date form and contact detail the package lists is tried one at a time against the real sensitive-text check, and so is each thing it says is not detected; the check only ever reports.

test:legal-package-app.about: The first-run statement, MOI Import (every marking shape, uploaded files, the saved plan) and the Squad Roster (fields, wording, every kind of finding, the Rank/MOS finding) through the real page.

test:legal-package-rooms.about: A real two-page study room walked through every state, reading the network-boundary panel on the host and the joiner in each.

test:legal-package-content.about: The shipped curriculum content, an inventory of every network primitive in the source, the guest-page server's routes, the ATO/NIPRNet statements and the release-checklist facts.

claims.finding: A bare (S) or (C) portion mark at the start of a line is NOT stopped when the pasted text also contains a lettered list item such as '(A) ...' or '(B) ...'. The check then reads (S) and (C) as list labels - a deliberate rule so that mnemonics like SALUTE's '(S) Size' and MARCH's '(C) Circulation' do not stop an import - so '(A) Alpha' followed by '(S) The unit departs.' passes with no finding. (TS), (CUI), spelled-out levels and any mark containing // are still stopped in the same text, and a lone '(S)' line stops as the package says. A real marked document that also uses lettered subparagraphs can therefore pass the check on its (S) and (C) marks; the sentence overstates.
claims.note: The other half of the sentence (any portion mark containing //) is LP-194 and holds.
